messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Cc: 
Date: 2027-09-29T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Role mapping proposal and QBR action list

Team —

Attached is the first-pass role-mapping proposal for the Platform org (org-map_v3.pdf) plus a short QBR action list focused on communications and OKR checkpoints (see bullets below). This is intended to be a concise package we can circulate to execs by EOD tomorrow. High-level objectives:
- Clarify ownership for the Serving Runtime & Ops pillars to reduce handoffs during incidents.
- Consolidate two small infra squads into a single Platform Reliability squad to improve on-call coverage.
- Add a Product Manager for Cost & Economics under Platform to lead Redwood Optimize integrations.

Quick asks from each of you by EOD today: 1) Flag anything you think is incorrect factually in the org map; 2) Suggest wording changes for the external-facing comm (tone, risk language); 3) Confirm we can commit to the timeline in slide note 3 of the QBR deck.

Proposed QBR action list (short):
- Monday: internal leadership review + sign-off on final comm framing.
- Tuesday: legal/HR redline check on role descriptions and transition language.
- Wednesday: send cascade email to affected squads with manager 1:1s scheduled in the following week.
- Thursday (QBR readout): exec summary slides + two talking points on how this ties to our H2 OKRs (customer reliability + cost/unit).

I've included a baseline draft of the comm text in roles-change-summary.docx and a link to a short drive deck. No surprises in the staffing counts — this is about consolidation and clearer ownership.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
VP, Platform
Redwood Inference

Attachments: org-map_v3.pdf (diagram), roles-change-summary.docx (draft comms), qbr-slide-deck.pptx (slides)

Subject: Re: Role mapping proposal and QBR action list

Grace —

Thanks for pulling this together, high level looks solid. A few quick notes inline:
1) On the Platform Reliability merge: can we add a short paragraph about how on-call rotation will change (hours, overlap, escalation path)? That will help CS and Sales with customer escalations.
2) For the Cost & Economics PM: suggest we frame it as "Product Lead, Cost " rather than "Manager" — it reads as more strategic in the external comm.
3) Tone: the draft reads a bit heavy on "rationalization" — recommend softer language like "streamlining" and call out protections for impacted ICs (re-training, redeployment).

I've attached two inline comments to the org-map (see link) and left a second slide note in the QBR deck suggesting we add a one-sentence ROI estimate for the consolidation.

-Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Product Operations
